questions.question: Loading and unloading students from a bus:

options.text: Is simple and does not need supervision.
Can be dangerous and must be supervised.
Can be done without the bus driver present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be dangerous and must be supervised.
questions.explanation: More students die during loading or unloading than while riding the bus. Bus drivers must follow safety rules during loading and unloading. This must always be supervised.

questions.question: ABS helps you:

options.text: Lock up your wheels.
Keep your wheels from locking up.
Count the number of students boarding the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your wheels from locking up.
questions.explanation: Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) stops your wheels from locking up when you brake hard on a slippery surface.

questions.question: When operating a school bus, mirrors should be adjusted:

options.text: During the drive.
Before you start driving.
After the drive is completed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before you start driving.
questions.explanation: Properly adjusted mirrors are critical for safe bus operation. Always check each mirror before you drive.

questions.question: If the driving test route does not include a railroad crossing, you:

options.text: Will not have to do anything related to a crossing.
May have to explain how you would cross railroad tracks.
Will have to take a different route.

questions.correctAnswerText: May have to explain how you would cross railroad tracks.
questions.explanation: If your test route does not include a railroad crossing, the examiner may ask you to explain what you would do at a simulated crossing.

questions.question: During the driving test at a railroad crossing, you should:

options.text: Pass another vehicle on the tracks if it is going too slow.
Get out of the vehicle to check for a train.
Not change gears while your vehicle is on the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not change gears while your vehicle is on the tracks.
questions.explanation: Do not stop, change gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes while any part of your vehicle is on railroad tracks.

questions.question: When driving a school bus, mirrors should be adjusted:

options.text: During the drive.
Before you start driving.
By the students.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before you start driving.
questions.explanation: Always check that all mirrors are properly adjusted before you operate a school bus.

questions.question: When students are picked up by a school bus:

options.text: Students should wait at a designated bus stop.
The driver should stop to pick up students walking to a designated bus stop.
Parents can choose where the bus stops are located.

questions.correctAnswerText: Students should wait at a designated bus stop.
questions.explanation: Bus drivers can only pick up students at official stops set by school officials.

questions.question: During the driving test, the examiner will score you on:

options.text: How well you speak.
How quickly you reach your destination.
Your general driving behavior.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your general driving behavior.
questions.explanation: The examiner will score you on specific driving skills and general driving behavior. You must drive safely, obey all traffic rules, and not cause an accident or traffic violation.

questions.question: If there is a fire on a school bus, students:

options.text: Must be evacuated.
Should stay on the bus but move away from the fire.
Should stay in their seats.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must be evacuated.
questions.explanation: If a school bus catches fire or might catch fire, the driver must get all students off the bus right away.

questions.question: The overhead rearview mirror is located:

options.text: On the right side of a bus.
On the steering wheel of a bus.
Above the windshield inside a bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Above the windshield inside a bus.
questions.explanation: On a school bus, the overhead inside rearview mirror is mounted above the windshield on the driver's side. Use this mirror to watch students inside the bus.

questions.question: How often should you do a pre-trip inspection?

options.text: Use a different method each time to check different items.
Use the same method each time to avoid forgetting anything.
Once in a while.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the same method each time to avoid forgetting anything.
questions.explanation: Do your pre-trip inspection the same way every time. This helps you remember all the steps and makes sure you don't miss anything.

questions.question: Where is the overhead rearview mirror located?

options.text: On the outside left of the bus.
On the outside right of the bus.
Above the windshield inside the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Above the windshield inside the bus.
questions.explanation: The overhead rearview mirror is mounted above the windshield on the driver's side inside the bus.

questions.question: Where is the overhead inside rearview mirror on a school bus?

options.text: Above the windshield on the driver's side.
Above the door across from the driver.
Above the emergency door in the rear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Above the windshield on the driver's side.
questions.explanation: The overhead inside rearview mirror should be mounted above the windshield on the driver's side. Use it to watch what students are doing inside the bus.

questions.question: What should you do at a railroad crossing during the driving test?

options.text: Pass another vehicle on the tracks if it is moving too slowly.
Change lanes while on the tracks.
Do not change gears while on the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not change gears while on the tracks.
questions.explanation: While any part of your vehicle is on railroad tracks, you must not stop, change gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes.

questions.question: What should you do if your bus stalls on railroad tracks?

options.text: Get everyone out of the bus and move far away from it.
Keep everyone inside and try to wave down the train to stop it.
Keep everyone inside and wait for help.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get everyone out of the bus and move far away from it.
questions.explanation: If the bus stalls on railroad tracks, get everyone out immediately and off the tracks. Move away from the tracks at an angle, away from any oncoming train.

questions.question: Where should students wait to be picked up by a school bus?

options.text: At a designated bus stop.
Anywhere, and the driver will pick them up.
Wherever the parents choose.

questions.correctAnswerText: At a designated bus stop.
questions.explanation: Pick up and drop off students only at designated stops that the school district has approved.

questions.question: What must a driver do when exiting a bus?

options.text: Never touch the handrail.
Keep contact with the handrail.
Move quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep contact with the handrail.
questions.explanation: When exiting the vehicle, face the vehicle and keep three points of contact with it at all times. For a bus, you must keep contact with the handrail. Exiting incorrectly may cause you to fail the basic vehicle control skills test.

questions.question: What should you check about the pedals before a trip?

options.text: The brake pedal sticks.
The gas pedal is loose.
The grooved pedal surface is not worn smooth.

questions.correctAnswerText: The grooved pedal surface is not worn smooth.
questions.explanation: Check that nothing is under or around the pedals that blocks them. Make sure the pedals work properly and that their grooved surfaces are not worn smooth.

questions.question: Before evacuating a bus due to a hazard, what should a driver do?

options.text: Ask the students if they want to leave.
Tell the dispatcher about the situation.
Take time to decide if evacuation is needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell the dispatcher about the situation.
questions.explanation: If you have time, contact your dispatcher before evacuating to explain what is happening. Make the evacuation decision quickly.

questions.question: What do crossover mirrors help the driver see?

options.text: The front bumper danger zones.
The rear bumper.
The left side of the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front bumper danger zones.
questions.explanation: Crossover mirrors help you see the danger zone directly in front of the bus. They also show the danger zones on the left and right sides of the bus, from the front to the service door.
